👉 **1. Look at the very first card at the top.** It has a deliberately huge title, a long description, and lots of tags. Check that the **title wraps neatly**, the **description is trimmed to a few lines** (so one rambling page can't dominate the list), and the **many tags wrap onto multiple rows** instead of overflowing.

👉 **2. Scroll down through the whole list.** With dozens of bookmarks, does it stay comfortable to browse, or does anything feel unwieldy?

👉 **3. With this large list, type in the search box** (e.g. `#reading`, or a word). Confirm it narrows down instantly even with many items.

A couple of decisions I'd like your reaction to, for the "large collection" case:
- **Long descriptions are trimmed to three lines on the card**; the full text is always kept and shown when you open Edit. Is trimming on the card the right call, or would you rather see the whole thing?
- **The list simply grows and scrolls** — there are no pages to click through. For a personal collection I judged one continuous, searchable list is friendlier than paging. Does that match how you'd want to browse a large collection?
